findings.location: build/web/claude/liturgy/roman-rite/postconciliar/roman-missal-third-edition-en-us-2011/propers/temporal/pc-s51-twenty-fifth-sunday-in-ordinary-time-year-a.md, whole document: nothing between the title block (lines 5-14) and the first section (line 16) stands for the PDF's Contents on p. 1
findings.problem: The study PDF opens with a Contents list of its eleven sections with page numbers. tools/web-edition (line 1099) deletes \tableofcontents, and neither the Markdown nor the site layout supplies any replacement. The published page is about 54,000 px tall at a 1280 px viewport and about 74,000 px tall at 500 px. It has 11 h2 and 51 h3 headings and no in-page navigation. Every heading carries an id, so nothing is unreachable by link, and the loss is navigation apparatus rather than text. guidance/web-editions.md neither declares this omission nor gives a reason for it, and the generate-web audit lists it only as an item for the reviewer.
findings.required_result: Either the canonical web edition offers in-page navigation equivalent to the PDF's Contents, or the decision to drop print navigation from long studies is recorded in guidance/web-editions.md where a reviewer will meet it. For the first, the converter could emit a [TOC] marker for an entrypoint that requests \tableofcontents, and the site's already-enabled toc extension would render it as a linked list of the sections.

findings.location: build/web/claude/liturgy/roman-rite/postconciliar/roman-missal-third-edition-en-us-2011/propers/temporal/pc-s51-twenty-fifth-sunday-in-ordinary-time-year-a.md lines 258-268, 320-330 and 386-396 (the three 'The four senses of this interpretation' blocks), and line 13 (the title-block subtitle); PDF pp. 17-18, 23 and 29
findings.problem:
The source sets the four senses as a description list (fourSenses in format.tex). The PDF therefore prints each label (Literal., Allegorical., Moral., Anagogical.) as a bold term with its text in a hanging indent. The converter writes each label as plain text followed by a two-space Markdown hard break. On the site that break is lost: render_source_page runs rewrite_links, which calls rstrip() on every line (tools/public-alpha, line 2968) before rendering, so the trailing spaces are gone first. In headless Chromium the rendered page carries no
in
at all. Each label runs straight into its paragraph at body weight, for example 'Literal. A landowner hires workers at five hours of one day…'. The generate-web note that each label is 'followed by a line break' is true only of scripts/_markdown_render.py on its own. The same stripping joins the two lines of the subtitle at line 13, which does no harm. Nothing is lost or confusable: all four senses are present, named, in order, each in its own paragraph under its own h3. But the one structure the three-documents contract requires of every interpretation is the one place where the source's distinction between label and body is dropped rather than adapted.
findings.required_result: On the published page, the four sense labels carry a weight or structure that survives the site's page path, so that each interpretation's senses can be scanned as easily as in the PDF. For example, the converter could write each description term as a bold run-in label, '**Literal.** …' (the form the tracked gpt proper editions already use and the site already renders), or the site could stop stripping Markdown hard breaks.

observations.note: The \multicolumn handling that guidance/web-editions.md declares deliberate puts each dossier's full-width prose note into the Textual unit column. On the site that column is about 220 of the table's 632 px at a 1280 px viewport, so the longest note (Isaiah, about 120 words) becomes a tall, narrow cell beside three empty columns. The guidance's reasoning weighs the header mismatch but not this narrow measure, which this dossier's long notes make conspicuous. The text is complete and readable, and this is recorded for the owner of that decision.

observations.location: tools/public-alpha rewrite_links (line 2968), which every web/ page passes through in render_source_page
observations.note: rewrite_links strips trailing whitespace from every Markdown line before rendering, so any two-space hard break is silently lost on the site. 16 tracked editions under web/ contain such lines, for example web/gpt/liturgy/roman-rite/1962/reference/assembling-the-mass.md with 253 lines and web/claude/liturgy/roman-rite/1962/propers/temporal/57-seventeenth-after-pentecost.md with 13. The converter's render audit uses scripts/_markdown_render.py alone and not the site's rewrite step, so a construct that depends on whitespace passes the audit and still changes on the page. This looks like a missing criterion in the converter audit or the site's verification, not something this conversion can repair.

observations.location: build/web/claude/liturgy/roman-rite/postconciliar/roman-missal-third-edition-en-us-2011/propers/temporal/pc-s51-twenty-fifth-sunday-in-ordinary-time-year-a.md lines 488-490 ('## References' followed by a standalone <span id="sec:references">)
observations.note: In sections/90-apparatus.tex, \label{sec:references} follows the starred References heading and its \addcontentsline instead of sitting on the heading. It therefore converts to an empty span in its own paragraph, while the heading takes the auto-generated id 'references'. Every other sec: label became its heading's own id. Nothing links to either id, so nothing is broken.

summary: Independent cold review of the canonical web conversion build/web/claude/liturgy/roman-rite/postconciliar/roman-missal-third-edition-en-us-2011/propers/temporal/pc-s51-twenty-fifth-sunday-in-ordinary-time-year-a.md, SHA-256 2bd7f5908e264581a4e66b209dc825266d43b51c688d4887ddea77ff4cd3586d. That is the hash research/web-artifact.json records and the one the packet's REVIEW_INPUTS seal names. The file on disk has that hash, and regenerating it with tools/web-edition into scratch reproduces those bytes exactly. I checked it against the ten research components of DOCUMENT_ROOT, all 26 of whose render inputs match research/artifacts.json. I also checked it against the reviewed study PDF (SHA-256 fd3a4d13f7bb980bbe3bb6025dac194997add5bf40a9f53eb4bced31af81dcb8, 39 pp.), guidance/web-editions.md and the schema-2 contract. Verdict: PASS, with two advisories and three observations and no blocking defect. I compared the extracted text of the PDF with the Markdown word by word (20,855 PDF words against 20,364). Every difference falls in one of these places: the Contents page (WEB-001), running heads and folios, the order in which the extractor reads table cells, line-end hyphenation, bullets and ellipsis tokens, and the title and subject that the converter prints from the PDF metadata. No word of the study is missing or added. All 135 Latin spans in the source appear verbatim. All five bracketed-italic unappointed half-verses survive, including the Acts 16:14 clause the generate-web stage restored. There are 34 verse superscripts, which matches the appointed verses. The dates in the chronology table match the generated projection. The whole-formulary interpretations keep their own h2 boundaries and each closes with its four senses. The comparison, date, branch and map tables are well formed (12x3, 9x4, 18x4 and 11x5 rows by columns). The heading hierarchy is 1 h1, 11 h2 and 51 h3 with no skipped level. All eleven proper-<element-key> anchors and ten sec: anchors are present, and the 64 ids are unique. All three external links answer HTTP 200. There is no TeX debris and no production metadata: no model, effort, run or provenance field. The revision timestamp 2026-09-19T18:27:31Z and the CC BY 4.0 colophon are both present and match the PDF. Only the canonical study is converted, with no concise or homily prose. Browser review: I rendered the sealed bytes, in scratch only, through the site's own page path (tools/public-alpha rewrite_links and render_page, the release layout and site.css). I inspected the result in headless Chromium at 1280 px and at 500 px, the smallest viewport headless allows. There is no page-level horizontal overflow, and the tables scroll inside themselves at narrow width. That render showed that the site path strips the two-space hard breaks the converter relies on. That is the new evidence in WEB-002. Limits: I did not run the full public-preview build, because it renders only tracked web/. I did no screen-reader or true 390 px phone test, and the screenshots are excerpt pages that share the page chrome. I edited nothing I reviewed.
